request.deadline: 12 months, with milestones at weeks 6, 12, 13, 16, 18, 24, 26, 39, and 52
deliverables: Four programs: Maintenance Fund, Maintainer Development program, CodeForUs bounty program, and Ecosystem Activation Reserve
Two advisory councils chartered with members named, COI policies signed, first meeting held, and charters published on-chain by week 6
dOSPO legal entity constituted as a 501(c)(3) public charity with governance documents published and operator agreement executed by week 24
Quarterly outcome reports for all active programs published on-chain with Mill Law Firm financial review attached
Dependency audit, SBOMs, centrality scores, bus factor assessments, and coverage gap analysis for Cardano OSS stack
First retainer cohort selected with published rubric scores, signed agreements, and on-chain disbursements
Public CHAOSS-aligned health dashboard for funded projects
End-of-term portfolio review with financial audit attached
request.recipient: Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting as sole Article II.7.5 administrator at treasury withdrawal, with Mill Law Firm designated as independent financial auditor.
request.what: Establish a one-year independent Cardano dOSPO and Open Maintenance Framework program to manage open source sustainability funds, advisory councils, a public charity target entity, maintenance retainers, maintainer development, bounties, and ecosystem activation programs.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 4,094,000 ADA over 12 months for a revised Cardano dOSPO and OMF program.
Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting is designated as the sole Article II.7.5 funds administrator effective at the moment of treasury withdrawal.
Mill Law Firm is designated as independent financial auditor for the full term on a quarterly cadence.
The advisory councils will provide published feedback before each disbursement, but final allocation authority remains with the designated administrator.
The proposal says a dedicated dOSPO legal entity structured as a U.S. 501(c)(3) public charity will be formed by Month 6, subject to legal processes and governance.
The Maintenance Fund will deploy 2,000,000 ADA over 12 months to fund high-risk Cardano open source infrastructure selected through dependency centrality and bus-factor analysis.

The proposer claims his track record includes serving as Senior Manager of Open Source Governance and Head of OSPO at Intersect and building Cardano open source governance functions from the ground up.

The proposal claims the dOSPO and OMF whitepapers were developed with experts from Bitergia, CHAOSS, Apache Software Foundation, Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust, Intersect, Andamio Platform, Modus Create, Leadingbit Solutions, and the Chinstrap Community.
The proposal targets 15 or more high-centrality projects funded by Month 12 and 40% of top-50 dependencies funded by Month 12.
The proposer claims the program can be shut down or the administrator replaced through an on-chain Info Action and commits to sponsoring such an Info Action if requested by 15 or more DReps.

summary: The document proposes a large one-year treasury-funded open source sustainability program administered initially by Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting, with advisory councils, quarterly reporting, legal entity formation, financial review, dependency-based maintenance funding, and stated governance replaceability mechanisms.
